Design spec · TW Live orders

TW Live order details (7-Eleven Store-to-Store)

TW Live orders (Order group, Order group with Buy Now lots, Buy Now with several quantities) are paid by credit/debit card and delivered by 7-Eleven Store-to-Store: the seller generates a shipping code, drops the parcel at any 7-Eleven, the buyer collects it at the store they chose. This handover covers the buyer and seller order details page (ODP) for that method: every state, its copy and button, how the order moves between states, and the flows opened from it (ship out, change store, cancel, change to meetup).

TW · Order group, Live mixed, Buy Now (Live) Draft · 2026-10-19 Source: partial — Fulfilment order page, SF Express drop-off model

Contents

01 · Read first02 · Components used03 · Layout structure04 · Diff from baseline05 · Interaction mechanics06 · States07 · Meet-up after Change to meetup08 · Desktop web09 · Cross-screen state machine10 · Checkpoints

It reuses the existing Fulfilment ODP. Only what is different for TW Live is described here.

01

Read first
  • One method, three shapes. Only the three Live shapes get Store-to-Store. A single item or a cart in TW still gets 7-Eleven Cash on Delivery. The methods do not mix.
  • The buyer has already paid. So nothing in the unhappy flow cancels the order: it goes on hold and both sides are sent to Contact support (the button is inert for now). The only cancellations are the seller cancelling and the system auto-cancel.
  • The buyer cannot cancel a Live order. There is no buyer cancel entry and the buyer's copy has no "you can cancel" line.
  • TW rules that differ from SG: amounts are NT$ with no decimals, dates are 2026-06-24, 12:34pm (YYYY-MM-DD), no GST, no Carousell Plus banner, the buyer pays no platform fee, the seller's fee is 6.0% of each item's selling price, rounded to the nearest dollar per item.
  • 16 stages (table under "States"). Some copy is production's, some is from Figma, some is a draft with no design source (marked draft below and listed in Checkpoints).
  • Meet-up is reachable only through the seller's "Change to meetup" (a TW Live buyer can't pick meet-up at checkout). It follows SG's rules and SG's production copy, in TW formats (section "Meet-up after Change to meetup").
  • Return/refund is not part of this handover: the row shows at "Order collected" but goes nowhere yet.

02

Components used

All from the existing kit unless noted.

Buyer and seller order details

  • Import / source: components/cart/buyer/order-details.tsx (BuyerOrderDetails), components/cart/seller/order-details.tsx (SellerOrderDetails); desktop web components/cart/web/web-order-scenes.tsx
  • Native mapping: not documented
  • Props used on this screen: statusCardOverride (card per stage), primaryActionOverride (button per stage, null = no button), courierRowOverride / deliveryDetailsOverride (delivery rows), hideCancelOrder, cancelAsSheet, onChangeToMeetup, hideReturnRefund / onStartReturnRefund (inert), hidePlusBanner
  • All stage logic lives in lib/fulfilment/tw-store-to-store.ts and lib/fulfilment/odp-view.ts; the scenario hook is lib/fulfilment/use-fulfilment-scene.ts.

TwPickupStoreFlow (shared, new)

  • Import / source: components/recommerce/fulfilment/tw-pickup-store-flow.tsx
  • What it is: the one store picker for TW Live: saved stores with "Add pick-up store" pushed below them (Figma 4223:8307, alone at the top when nothing is saved) → Add pick-up store form (Figma 4477:29689) → 7-Eleven e-map → back to the form with the store filled → Save.
  • Props: open, savedStores, unavailableStoreId (left out of the saved list), onClose, onChosen(store, { recipient, phone }).
  • Used by: buyer "Choose another store", seller "Choose another store" (return store closed), the TW live wallet. 7-Eleven Cash on Delivery keeps its own picker (TwChooseStoreFlow).
  • Prototype convenience: tapping an empty Recipient or Mobile number field fills a sample (裴語燕, 0912345678). Not part of the spec.

TwInvoiceForm (existing, new meetup variant)

  • Source: components/recommerce/order/tw-invoice-form.tsx
  • Props used: role="seller", storeToStore for the ship-out page (Figma 4341:7142), meetup for the meet-up Confirm order page. Both share one layout; meetup changes the title and intro, replaces the Sender info section with an email-only "Your details" (no name or mobile, and only the email is validated) and sets the button text to Confirm order.

TwEmapScreens (one-off, new)

  • Source: components/recommerce/fulfilment/tw-emap.tsx
  • What it is: a redraw of 7-Eleven's own e-map (a third party's web page, Figma 4874:48973): city → district → street → store → map → ID reminder → store details → 確定門市. Its greens, blues and orange are 7-Eleven's colours, not Carousell tokens. Production opens the real e-map in a web view, so engineering does not build this screen.
  • Only 台北市 → 中山區 carries data; any other pick moves on with the same placeholder store.

CancelOrderFlow, sheet presentation

  • Source: components/cart/cancel-order-flow.tsx, prop presentation="sheet" (default "page" is production iOS's full-screen form, unchanged)
  • What it is: the seller cancel flow as a bottom sheet of reasons (Figma 4342:7674) followed by a modal "Cancel this order?" (Figma 4342:7690 draws this step as a sheet; the design call is a modal).

04

Diff from baseline
  • A new delivery method (seven-eleven-s2s) and payment method (card), both TW Live only.
  • Stages the status model can't express (the shared OrderStatus has one delivery_on_hold, one delivery_in_progress): the scene carries a twStage next to the status and normalises it whenever the status changes (a deep link status=delivery_on_hold always lands on "returning to seller").
  • Collecting is not completing. "Order collected" is delivery_completed; the buyer taps Order received (a confirm dialog first) or the order auto-completes after 2 days, then it is order_completed.
  • Auto-cancel exists here (6 and 4 days), and the buyer has no cancel.
  • TW formatting (NT$, YYYY-MM-DD, h:mma) is applied through a client-only display currency switched on after hydration, so SG output is never affected.

05

Interaction mechanics

N/A for gestures: there are no drags or swipes. Every stage change is an instant swap of the card, icon and button; nothing is animated by this work. The sheets use the kit's existing bottom-sheet slide-in (animate-in slide-in-from-bottom duration-300) and the e-map steps swap instantly. The "處理中，請稍後…" screen in the e-map auto-advances after 900 ms.

EntryWhat happens
Seller Ship order (Pending ship out)Ship-out form "Delivery details" (Figma 4341:7142): Sender info (Your name, Mobile number, Email, e-invoice fields), footer button Generate QR code. The first-time "Details, please" alert is not shown for Store-to-Store (it is on Cash on Delivery). On submit the stage becomes "Shipping code generated".
Seller Confirm order (meet-up, awaiting confirmation)The Confirm order page with e-invoice details (see "Confirm order page" under Meet-up), then the e-invoice consent.

Seller Choose another store (return store closed)Same flow. Picking one returns the stage to "returning to seller", and the return cards then name the chosen store.
Seller footer Cancel orderBottom sheet "Cancel order?": "Reason for cancellation" + 10 radio reasons + details box + Cancel order (disabled until a reason is picked; "Others" also needs text). Then a modal (not a sheet) "Cancel this order?" with "If you cancel too many orders, you won't be allowed to list with the 'Buy' button for a period of time.", Back / Cancel anyway. Then the order is cancelled for both sides. Reasons are production iOS's seller list.
Seller footer Change to meetupDialog "Change this order to meetup?" / "Delivery charges will be removed and your buyer will be notified" / Change to meet-up / Back. Delivery fee goes to NT$0 (total NT$415). The order becomes a meet-up order (see "Meet-up after Change to meetup").
Buyer Order received (Order collected)Confirm dialog, then the order completes.

Cancel and Change to meetup are only available before the shipping code is generated (Figma's cancellation window ends at the drop-off request). From "Shipping code generated" on, both are hidden.

07

Meet-up after Change to meetup

The seller's Change to meetup (only before the shipping code is generated) turns a Store-to-Store order into a meet-up order. This is the only way into meet-up for TW Live: a buyer can't pick it at checkout. Rules and copy are SG's, in TW formats; nothing here is TW-specific design.

  • Rules (same as SG): the seller has 3 days to confirm or the system cancels the order; once the meet-up date passes, the order auto-completes 9 days after the meet-up if nobody taps Order received.
  • Where and when to meet is agreed in chat. The app carries no meet-up location or time, only the deadlines below.
  • Copy: SG's production copy (OrderVisualizer). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, amounts NT$.
  • Money: the delivery fee is removed, so the sample total goes from NT$475 to NT$415; the seller's earnings stay NT$390 (6.0% fee).
  • Page layout (the meet-up template, same for buyer and seller, at every phase): a "Delivery details" section with one Meet up row (the delivery truck icon, the title "Meet up", then the meet-up locations as teal links), and no address, no name or phone, and no "Buyer's details". Production builds the address and buyer details from the delivery's logistics record, which a meet-up doesn't have.
- Status card
- Delivery details: Meet up, Location A / Location B / Location C (teal links)
- Counterparty (username, View profile) and the lots
- Payment summary / Earnings summary   (no delivery fee on the buyer's side)
- Order ID, order time
- Chat, Help center, Contact support, Cancel order
- Bottom button
  • SG meet-up uses the same page layout (its own dates and S$ amounts are unchanged).
  • Seller Cancel order: on a meet-up order the row stays enabled while the order waits for the seller to confirm, as production does (checkpoint 23). After the seller confirms the meet-up, it is disabled. Same on the app and desktop.

Confirm order page (e-invoice details)

The seller must give e-invoice details to confirm a meet-up order. Confirm order opens a page (app) with the e-invoice part of the ship-out page (Figma 4341:7142) and an intro that says what happens after confirming, instead of the usual confirm dialog.

  • Title: "Confirm order". Back arrow returns to the order page.
  • Intro (one paragraph, copy given by design): "Details below will be used to generate an invoice for the platform fee. Your buyer will be notified once you confirm, then you can arrange the meet-up in Chat."
  • Your details: email only. The ship-out page asks for name, mobile and email under "Sender info"; the meet-up page has a "Your details" heading with the Email field only (prefilled with the account email, required and validated). This is the email the e-invoice consent refers to.
  • E-invoice information: E-invoice type (Individual / Business / Donation) with Membership carrier / Mobile phone barcode / Citizen Digital Certificate ID, and the "FAQ about invoices" link. Same fields, validation and consent as the ship-out page.
  • Bottom bar: "Remember invoice details for next time" (checkbox), Confirm order, "By tapping on 'Confirm order' you agree to Carousell's Terms of Service and Privacy Policy".
  • On Confirm order: errors show on the empty or invalid fields; a valid form opens the "Requesting for e-invoice" consent; accepting it confirms the order (M2 Meet-up scheduled).
  • Desktop web: the same content in a modal ("Confirm order", the same intro, "Your details" with the email, the e-invoice information, Confirm order and the consent), opened by the Confirm order button instead of the old confirm dialog.

08

Desktop web

Desktop web follows the app on every TW Live state. It was checked state by state (all 16 Store-to-Store stages, both cancelled variants, the five meet-up phases, the tracking screen, the cancel flow and both e-invoice modals): the status cards, delivery rows, sections and buttons carry the same text. The differences are on purpose:

  • QR and store picker are modals: "View QR code" and "Choose another store" (buyer, and seller for the return store) open as modals on desktop, with the same content as the app. The e-map is the same redraw, inside the modal. Cash on Delivery keeps production's "only on the app" dialog.
  • Ship order opens a modal that mirrors the app page: "Delivery details", the same intro, "Sender info" (name, mobile, email), the e-invoice information, and Generate shipping code (the app says Generate QR code).
  • Confirm order on a meet-up order opens a modal with the same content as the app page (see "Confirm order page").
  • Cancel order is a modal of reasons with the "Cancel this order?" confirm on top (same reasons, same confirm copy and "Cancel anyway"); the app shows the reasons as a bottom sheet.
  • "See my Balance" is capitalised on desktop and "See my balance" on the app (each platform's own production wording).
  • Earnings summary (seller): desktop always lists Subtotal, Platform fee and Your earnings, with no expand or hide, as production's desktop order page does. "View breakdown" under Your earnings opens the Earnings breakdown as a modal (production's OrderDetailEarningsBreakdownModal), with the same rows as the app's Earnings breakdown page. The app shows Your earnings with "View breakdown" only, which opens that page. On both, the Platform fee row is a single line with the fee total (NT$ at 6.0% of each lot, rounded); there are no category lines under it. Desktop's e-invoice section matches the app: the invoice type is a row of chips, with the carrier radios below and the "FAQ about invoices" link. Desktop's Order info also has no "Last updated" row, as the app.
  • Order lists: the buyer's list shows one card per order, as the app. The seller's list stays a table (the desktop layout).
  • Cancel order and Change to meetup are hidden from "Shipping code generated" on, as on the app.

Order collectedBuyer taps Order received, or 2 days passOrder completed
Returning to sellerItem arrives at the seller's storeReturn ready to collect
Returning to sellerReturn store closesReturn store closed
Return store closedSeller picks another storeReturning to seller
Return store closed7 days pass, seller doesn't chooseAbandoned
Return ready to collectSeller collects the itemReturn collected

Timing rules (from the Figma timeline 4431:29506): 6 days from the order to ship out; 4 days from the code to drop off; delivery period; 7 days at the store; 2 days to auto-completion; cancellation window ends at the drop-off request. The buyer is reminded on days 3 and 6 when a store is closed; reminders are not built (they go in the notification section later), they only appear as text in the rules panel.

Not allowed on purpose: store-closed after the code is generated, or after the parcel arrived (production's state machine only allows StoreUnavailable from Initial, DeliveryStarted and Transporting).
